10: Picked Raquel Ellison (5337a14f) as the matching person.
16: Queried APX issues assigned to 5337a14f → empty.
17: Queried all issues assigned to 5337a14f → empty.
18: assignedIssues of 5337a14f → empty.
19: Queried all APX issues → found APX-4 (Raquel Vance), APX-5 (Raquel Ford), APX-8 (Leo Park).
20-21: Searched "offline sync" titles → only APX-4 and APX-5.
22: Final full scan.
Final answer: reported the mismatch, did not change anything, asked which of APX-4 or APX-5 to set.

This is "naming a near-miss as non-matching, or offering it as an alternative" — which is allowed under correct_absent. The solver did not say "APX-4 is the issue you're referring to." So it's not presented.

Also, did the solver act on anything? No writes, no state diff. So not incorrect.

The solver read Raquel Vance's statusLabel as "Heads down shipping" — consistent. The solver didn't read the description, but the decisive field (statusLabel) was read, and the mismatch was noted in the reasoning and the final answer.

Therefore the verdict: correct_absent. Exposed facts: empty (only for incorrect and presented). Mechanism: none.

The solver stopped without acting, having asked a clarifying question. For an absence test, "asking a clarifying question without acting is fine." So correct_absent.

Also double-check: the request presupposes a single issue ("the offline sync issue assigned to Rae Ellison") — singular. Two issues match on team + title, but both fail on the status condition of the assignee. So no target. The solver correctly concluded no match.

One more consideration: does asking "Which should I set to 3 — APX-4 or APX-5?" count as "offering one as an alternative" — allowed. Yes.
